metadata.title: Benchmarking Large Language Models in Code Generation: A Systematic Review

epistemology.epistemological_rationale: Statistical generalisability of benchmark performance across models requires a Positivist stance with quantitative evidence.
incompatible_concepts: Qualitative opinion surveys without code evaluation
epistemology.unit_of_analysis: Peer-reviewed empirical studies of LLM code generation

research_questions.text: What automated benchmarks are used in the literature to measure LLM code generation pass rates?

research_questions.required_evidence_type: Ablation delta tables and latency measurements
research_questions.text: What is the measured performance difference between dense retrieval and graph-boosted RAG for code synthesis?

research_questions.required_evidence_type: Reported limitations and threats to validity
research_questions.text: What limitations and threats to validity are most commonly reported in LLM code generation benchmarking studies?

exclusion.criterion: Position papers or non-peer-reviewed blog posts without empirical code evaluation
Studies focusing purely on natural language translation without code execution

inclusion.criterion: Presents a novel computational model, prompt architecture, or RAG pipeline for code generation
Evaluates performance quantitatively against public standard benchmark datasets
Reports at least one limitation or threat to validity
